accepted.question_text: Let X be a compact Kähler surface, let B be a ball in C^2, and let f: B^* -> X be a locally biholomorphic map from the punctured ball B^* = B \ {0}. The paper states that f extends meromorphically to a map \hat{f}: B -> X. If E := \hat{f}[0] is the full image of the origin under this extension, prove that E is an exceptional curve in X.
accepted.context_brief: Exceptional set of a puncture extension

evidence.quote: 2.3. Open Questions. Let X be a compact K¨ahler surface and let f : B∗ → X be a locally biholomorphic mapping of the punctured ball B∗ = B \ {0} into X. Then f extends meromorphically onto the whole ball B. The full image by the extension ˆf of the origin denote by E := ˆf[0].
Question 2.1 Prove that E is an exceptional curve in X.

accepted.question_text: In the setting of Theorem 2.4, let X be a compact infinitesimally homogeneous Kähler manifold, let D be a domain over a Stein manifold, and let f: D -> X be a locally biholomorphic map. The theorem gives a meromorphic extension \hat{f}: \hat{D} -> X to the envelope of holomorphy of D; let I denote the indeterminacy set of \hat{f}. Determine what can be said about the image \hat{f}[I].

evidence.quote: Theorem 2.4 Let X be a compact infinitesimally homogeneous K¨ahler manifold. Then every locally biholomorphic mapping f : D → X from a domain D over a Stein manifold into X extends to a locally biholomorphic mapping ˆf : Dˆ → X of the envelope of holomorphy Dˆ of D into X.
Question 2.2 What can be said about ˆf[I] in the conditions of Theorem 2.4?

accepted.question_text: Let H^k_n(r) = (Delta^n(1-r) x Delta^k) union (Delta^n x A^k(r,1)) be the Hartogs figure introduced in the paper, and let X be a compact or disk-convex complex manifold or complex space in the class P^-_k, with the stronger subclass G_k when appropriate. Is it true in all dimensions that every meromorphic map from H^k_n(r) to X extends to Delta^(n+k) minus a singular set A of Hausdorff (2n-1)-dimensional measure zero, with the stronger topological restrictions predicted in the G_k case when A is nonempty? In particular, should the three-dimensional extension theorem stated as Theorem 3.2 remain valid for equidimensional meromorphic maps in every dimension?

evidence.quote: General Conjecture. Meromorphic mappings from Hk_n(r) to compact (disk-convex) manifolds of class P^-_k should extend onto ∆n+k \ A where A is of Haussdorf (2n − 1)-dimensional measure zero. If the image manifold is from class Gk then A 6= ∅ should imply very restrictive conditions on the topology and complex structure of X (see results below).

Question 3.1 We conjecture that the analogous result should hold for meromorphic mappings in all dimensions. I.e. from Hk_n(r) to compact manifolds (and spaces) in the classes P^-_k and Gk. In particular, Theorem 3.2 should be true for meromorphic mappings between equidimensional manifolds in all dimensions.

accepted.question_text: As a first step toward the general conjecture on extension from Hartogs figures, prove the case of meromorphic extension from the four-dimensional Hartogs figure H^2_2(r) to a target manifold in the class G_2.

evidence.quote: Question 3.2 One can start proving the general conjecture (as in Question 3.1) by considering extension from H2_2(r) to a manifold of class G2.

accepted.question_text: Generalize Corollary 3.2 to all dimensions. In other words, for a compact affine n-fold whose universal cover is viewed as a domain over C^n with locally biholomorphic projection, determine whether pseudoconcavity of the covering domain at a boundary point forces the compact manifold to contain the higher-dimensional analogue of a spherical shell.

evidence.quote: Corollary 3.2 Let V be a compact affine 3-fold and let (V , π ˜ ) be its universal covering considered as a domain over C3 with locally biholomorphic projection π. Then if (V , π ˜ ) is pseudoconcave at some boundary point then V contains a spherical shell (of dimension 3).
Question 3.3 An analog of Corollary 3.2. in all dimensions seems to be an easier problem then the Question 3.1 in its whole generality.

accepted.question_text: Let X be a compact complex manifold carrying a plurinegative metric form, and let f: Delta^3 \ S -> X be a meromorphic map. Suppose A is the minimal closed subset of Delta^3 such that f extends meromorphically to Delta^3 \ A. Prove that each connected component of A is a complex curve.
accepted.context_brief: Structure of the singularity set in dimension 3

evidence.quote: Question 3.4 Let X is a compact complex manifold carrying a plurinegative metric form, and let f : ∆3 \ S → X is a meromorphic mapping. Suppose that A is a minimal closed subset of ∆3 such that f extends onto ∆3 \ A. Prove that each connected component of A is a complex curve.

accepted.question_text: Suppose pi: X -> Delta is a complex deformation of compact complex manifolds and every nearby noncentral fiber X_t for t != 0 has the meromorphic extension property, meaning that every meromorphic map from a domain in a Stein manifold extends meromorphically to the envelope of holomorphy. Must the central fiber X_0 also have the meromorphic extension property?
accepted.context_brief: Closedness of meromorphic extension under deformation

evidence.quote: We say that a complex manifold X possesses a meromorphic extension property if for every domain D in Stein manifold every meromorphic mapping f : D → X meromorphically extends onto the envelope of holomorphy of D.
Question 4.1 Suppose all Xt for t 6= 0 possed meromorphic extension property (as, for example, K¨ahler manifolds). Does X0 possesses it as well?

accepted.question_text: If the central fiber X_0 of a complex deformation has the meromorphic extension property, does every nearby fiber X_t also have the meromorphic extension property for t close to 0?
accepted.context_brief: Openness of meromorphic extension under deformation

evidence.quote: We say that a complex manifold X possesses a meromorphic extension property if for every domain D in Stein manifold every meromorphic mapping f : D → X meromorphically extends onto the envelope of holomorphy of D.
Question 4.2 If X0 possesses a mer. ext. prop. does Xt possesses it for t close to zero?

accepted.question_text: Let D be a domain in CP^3 that covers a compact complex threefold X, and let Lambda = CP^3 \ D be the complement. Proposition 5.1 proves that if Lambda is locally a finite union of two-dimensional submanifolds, then Lambda is a finite union of lines. Prove an analogue of this statement assuming only that the 2-dimensional Hausdorff measure h_2(Lambda) is finite; in that setting, determine whether the components of Lambda can only be lines and isolated points.

evidence.quote: Proposition 5.1 Suppose a domain D ⊂ CP3 covers a compact complex threefold X. Case 1. If the complement Λ = CP3 \ D is locally a finite union of two-dimensional submanifolds, then Λ is a union of finitely many lines.
Question 5.1 Prove an analog of the Case 1 of Theorem 5.1 assuming only that h2(Λ) is finite. In that case the components of Λ could be lines and points.

accepted.question_text: Let D be a domain in CP^3 with complement Lambda = CP^3 \ D, and assume Lambda is locally a union of four-dimensional submanifolds. Must every connected component of Lambda be either a complex hypersurface or a CR submanifold of CR dimension 1? Can components occur that are not CR submanifolds at all? If the CR components do exist, must they be Levi-flat?

evidence.quote: Question 5.2 Suppose that the complement Λ = CP3 \ D is locally a union of four-dimensional submanifolds. Are all components of Λ necessariry either complex hypersurfaces or CR-manifolds of CR-dimension one? Or, one can have components which are not CR-submanifolds? Are those CR-submanifolds Levi-flat?

accepted.question_text: Can every complex surface be embedded as a subdomain of some disk-convex complex surface?

evidence.quote: Question 6.1 Can every complex surface be imbedded as a subdomain into a disk-convex complex surface?

accepted.question_text: The paper lists several notions of disk-convexity: the original condition from Definition 6.1, a version using holomorphic maps from arbitrary bordered Riemann surfaces, a sequential compactness condition for analytic disks, and the analogous sequential condition for families of bordered Riemann surfaces. What is the precise relationship among these notions? Are they all equivalent, and if not, which implications between them are valid?

evidence.quote: In some cases another notions of “disk-convexity” are needed:
Question 6.2 What is the relation between all these notions and that defined in Definition 6.1? Are they equivalent? Of course there are some obvious implications.

accepted.question_text: Let D be the two-sheeted cover of Delta^2 \ R^2 described in the paper, so that D is a nonschlicht domain over C^2. Does there exist a compact complex manifold X and a holomorphic or meromorphic map f: D -> X that separates points of D? The paper notes that any such target X cannot carry a plurinegative metric form, so possible examples would have to start in complex dimension greater than 3.
accepted.context_brief: Maps separating points on a nonschlicht domain

evidence.quote: Question 7.1 Let the complex manifold D is defined as two-sheeted cover of ∆2 \ R2, i.e. D is a ”nonschlicht” domain over C2. Does there exist a compact complex manifold X and a holomorphic (meromorphic) mapping f : D → X which separates points?
Note that the results of this paper imply that such X if exists cannot possed a plurinegative metric form. Thus examples could occur starting from dim X > 3.

accepted.question_text: Fix a compact complex manifold X, an integer k, a constant R > 0, and a constant C_1. Let J_R be the class of meromorphic maps f: Delta^k -> X such that the norm of the differential satisfies ||Df|| > R everywhere and the volume of the image f(Delta^k) is at most C_1. Prove that there is a constant C_2 = C_2(X, R, C_1) such that the volume of the graph Gamma_f is at most C_2 for every f in J_R.
accepted.context_brief: Bounding graph volume from image volume and differential lower bounds

evidence.quote: Question 7.2 Consider a class JR of meromorphic mappings f : ∆k → X, X being compact, such that (a) kDfk > R > 0. Here kDfk denotes the norm of the differential of f; (b) Vol(f(∆k) 6 C1 for all f ∈ JR. Prove that there is a constant C2 = C2(X, R, C1) such that Vol(Γf ) 6 C2 for all f ∈ JR.

accepted.question_text: Let f: Delta^*_k -> X be a meromorphic map from a punctured k-dimensional polydisk into a compact complex space X. If the volume of f(Delta^*_k) is finite, prove that f extends meromorphically across the puncture to the origin.
accepted.context_brief: Finite-volume extension from a punctured polydisk

evidence.quote: Question 7.3 Let f : ∆k_* → X be a meromorphic mapping from a punctured polydisk into a compact complex space X. Suppose that Volf(∆k_* ) < ∞. Prove that f meromorphically extends to zero.

accepted.question_text: Let X = {X_t} be a deformation of compact complex surfaces. If every nearby fiber X_t with t != 0 contains a global spherical shell, must the central fiber X_0 also contain a global spherical shell?
accepted.context_brief: Persistence of global spherical shells under deformation

evidence.quote: Question 7.6 Let X = {Xt} be a deformation of compact complex surfaces. Suppose that Xt for t 6= 0 contain a global spherical shell. Does X0 contain a GSS?

accepted.question_text: Let F be a family of holomorphic or meromorphic maps from the unit polydisk Delta^(n+1) to a compact Kähler manifold X, or more generally to a target X in the class G_1. If F is equicontinuous on the Hartogs figure H^1_n(r), must F be equicontinuous on the whole polydisk Delta^(n+1)?

evidence.quote: Question 7.7 Let F be some family of holomorphic (meromorphic) mappings from the unit polydisk ∆n+1 to a compact K¨ahler manifold X (or X ∈ G1 more generally). Suppose that F is equicontinuous on the Hartogs figure H1_n(r). Will F be equicontinuous on ∆n+1?

needs_review.question_text_raw: Question 7.4 asks for a sharp logarithmic growth bound for the volume of the image of annuli under meromorphic maps f: Delta^(k+1)_* -> X in G_k, but the exponent formatting in the extracted PDF text is ambiguous.

evidence.quote: Question 7.4 Let f : ∆k+1_* → X ∈ Gk be a meromorphic map from punctured (k + 1)-disk into a compact complex space from class Gk. Prove that Vol(f(Ak(r, 1)) = O(log k k−1 ( 1 r )) provided k > 2. In particular for equidimensional maps f : ∆n_* → Xn one always should have Vol(f(An(r, 1)) = O(log n n−1 ( 1 r )).

needs_review.question_text_raw: Question 7.5 asks for two-way bounds between total graph volume and the graph volumes of restrictions to coordinate k-disks under annular control assumptions, but several slice and annulus notations are partially garbled in the extracted PDF text.

evidence.quote: Question 7.5 Fix some 0 < r < 1 and some constant R. Fix also a compact complex space X. Consider the following class FR of meromorphic mappings from f : ∆n → X: (1) Vol2n(Γf ∩ (An(r, 1) × X)) 6 R; (2) for every k-disk ∆k_z = {z} × ∆k( where z ∈ ∆n−k) Vol2k(Γfz ∩ Ak_z(r, 1) × X) 6 R. Prove that for any constant l there is a constant A such that for any f ∈ FR satisfying Vol2k(Γfz) 6 l for all restrictions fz of f onto the k-disks ∆k_z one has Vol2n(Γf ) 6 A. (b) Vice versa: for any constant a there is a constant L such that for any f ∈ FR such that Vol2n(Γf ) 6 a one has Vol2k(Γfs) 6 L for all ∆k_z.
